# Findings by archetype

The same campaigns as the [register](register.md), grouped by what they were run over. A registry-wide campaign appears under every archetype it covered.

## DeadCatBounce

| cite      | campaign                                                                                                                        | outcome       | verdict                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `§M7a`    | [M7a — the random-entry control arm: done](m7a-random-entry-control.md)                                                         | `mixed`       | DeadCatBounce's entry rule is measurably better than random at p = 0.012 while still losing money, which makes the loss one of costs, hold time or bracket geometry rather than of the entry.                                                                                     |
| `§M19.1`  | [M19.1 — compression as a condition, before it is an archetype](m19-1-compression-condition.md)                                 | `negative`    | The condition is real and consistently ordered across seven archetypes and two roots, and it still separates no better than four dimensions the campaign already had — a reason to keep M19 parked rather than to build it.                                                       |
| `§M27`    | [M27 — the registry-wide campaign: every archetype, every axis](m27-registry-campaign.md)                                       | `mixed`       | Bar size is the largest lever and the moving averages are nearly inert; four of six pass gate 1, three gate 2, one gate 3 — and what stops InsideBar is its bracket rather than its entry.                                                                                        |
| `§M27.4`  | [M27.4 — the sixteen strata that were never held out](m27-4-strata-held-out.md)                                                 | `mixed`       | The shortlist decays by about the same amount in every stratum, it is not noise, and InsideBar's DIRECTIONAL cell turns out to have two larger siblings.                                                                                                                          |
| `§M27.5`  | [M27.5 — the regime threshold, calibrated rather than swept blind](m27-5-regime-threshold.md)                                   | `calibration` | The regime threshold is fitted rather than guessed, which restores the per-contract sample in most places but not everywhere; cross-resolution rows are not twins.                                                                                                                |
| `§M27.7`  | [M27.7 — time of day: swept, never read, and the artefact is in the wrong phase](m27-7-time-of-day.md)                          | `mixed`       | Against a matched random entry the edge is in the quiet phases; the forced flat lands in AFTERNOON rather than CLOSE, and InsideBar's CLOSE stratum is empty by construction.                                                                                                     |
| `§M27.8`  | [M27.8 — volume: one form, one cut, and the answer is the cut's](m27-8-volume.md)                                               | `mixed`       | Which volume state helps is decided by the form and the cut rather than by volume; held out it is a coin flip, and `NORMAL` is the best cell under two forms of three.                                                                                                            |
| `§M28.9`  | [M28.9 — the survivor, read for tradeability rather than for rank](m28-9-survivor-tradeability.md)                              | `mixed`       | Held out, one cell in thirteen across the registry returns its own drawdown; the binding constraint is net-to-drawdown rather than profit factor, and the edge is absent from 2026.                                                                                               |
| `§M28.12` | [M28.12 — the bracket decomposition, read across the registry](m28-12-bracket-decomposition.md)                                 | `mixed`       | One archetype in seven has a bracket that pays for itself held out; InsideBar's stop is nearly inert and its forced flat hands back about 90% of what the bracket earns.                                                                                                          |
| `§M28.13` | [M28.13 — the registry read through an account, and the assumption that turned out to be a parameter](m28-13-account-read.md)   | `mixed`       | Survival is not the question and reading it as one inverts the answer; the binding constraint is position size rather than the strategy, and the excursion order was an assumption and is now `excursion_order`.                                                                  |
| `§M28.14` | [M28.14 — every stratum against its unfiltered twin, and the cell that survives it](m28-14-stratum-cross-read.md)               | `mixed`       | The clock separates the registry while volume and trend mostly do not; the midday cell clears four gates and the flatten is still what earns it.                                                                                                                                  |
| `§M28.16` | [M28.16 — the ten consistent cells through the matched null, and what a consistency score is worth](m28-16-consistent-cells.md) | `mixed`       | Four cells clear p = 0.05 on both roots — three OpeningRange's and one InsideBarTrailing's midday cell — and a consistency score does not order the null result, correlating −0.132 with it.                                                                                      |
| `§M29`    | [M29 — the maximum hold time: the one axis whose best value is off on every archetype](m29-maximum-hold-time.md)                | `negative`    | Capping a trade's length is a cost on all seven archetypes and the cost is monotone in the cap; the selection window picks a paying rung zero times in seven, and the two ported archetypes hold too briefly to reach one at all.                                                 |
| `§M30`    | [M30 — volume and regime re-cut across the registry, and what the raw pair was reporting](m30-volume-regime-recut.md)           | `mixed`       | Re-cutting turns three of six volume dimensions from inert to consistent and sorts the regime dimension by what each archetype is; almost none of the new cells makes money, and the raw regime labels agree with a calibrated cut about a fifth of the time at a lookback of 50. |

| `§M28.1`  | [M28.1 — OpeningRange: built, swept, and the first archetype through three gates](m28-1-openingrange-swept.md)                      | `positive` | The first archetype ever to pass gates 1 to 3: the stop mode splits it into a half that always passes and a half that always fails, and gate 4 is a sample-size verdict rather than a failure.                                                                                    |
| `§M28.2`  | [M28.2 — the deferral list, built: three entry mechanisms, one stop axis, and a null over levels](m28-2-deferral-list.md)           | `mixed`    | The breakout reproduces §M28.1 and gains a level null; the fade fails gate 1 everywhere and is parked; the retest has no verdict because its gate-2 pass measures `ambiguity_policy` rather than a strategy.                                                                      |
| `§M28.4`  | [M28.4 — settling the ambiguous bar instead of bounding it](m28-4-settling-ambiguous-bar.md)                                        | `tooling`  | Minute bars settle 17% of ambiguous bars and all of them against the assumption, which bounds the retest's profit factor from above; it stays a diagnostic and never enters `nqbt/sim/`.                                                                                          |
| `§M28.5`  | [M28.5 — the fade's bracket, tightened: monotone the other way, and zero of 15,360](m28-5-fade-bracket.md)                          | `negative` | The stop axis is monotone across the whole of 0.02 to 1.0 of the range width because the stop sits inside the bar the order fills on; the held-out test reproduces gate 1 exactly.                                                                                                |
| `§M28.6`  | [M28.6 — the rejection: the fade's level, the retest's order type, and no break at all](m28-6-rejection-spec.md)                    | `spec`     | Four modes and three properties, built from the fade's level and the retest's order type with no new machinery.                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `§M28.7`  | [M28.7 — the rejection, swept: every profitable cell is one the fill assumption decides](m28-7-rejection-swept.md)                  | `negative` | Profitability tracks the fill assumption and nothing else — every profitable cell in 245,760 is one the assumption decides, which is a stronger negative than the retest's no-verdict.                                                                                            |
| `§M28.8`  | [M28.8 — the range as a cross: every anchor by every length, and the hour that was missing](m28-8-range-cross.md)                   | `mixed`    | The anchor and the length are one cell rather than two axes; the one-hour cash range sits on a plateau with no excess on it, and §M28's 5, 15 and 30 turn out to have been the right set.                                                                                         |
| `§M28.9`  | [M28.9 — the survivor, read for tradeability rather than for rank](m28-9-survivor-tradeability.md)                                  | `mixed`    | Held out, one cell in thirteen across the registry returns its own drawdown; the binding constraint is net-to-drawdown rather than profit factor, and the edge is absent from 2026.                                                                                               |
| `§M28.10` | [M28.10 — the geometry denominated in trailing follow-through: no, and the reason is arithmetic](m28-10-follow-through-geometry.md) | `negative` | Normalising the geometry against trailing follow-through does not restore 2026 on either root; follow-through fell 18% while the median range rose 136%, so the width is what is worth normalising against.                                                                       |
| `§M28.11` | [M28.11 — the two truncated bracket axes, swept to their end](m28-11-truncated-bracket-axes.md)                                     | `negative` | Both axes are now swept to their end: the wider stop fails the acceptance cell, costs two thirds of net-to-drawdown, and lowers the excess over a permuted range as `session_close_share` doubles.                                                                                |
| `§M28.12` | [M28.12 — the bracket decomposition, read across the registry](m28-12-bracket-decomposition.md)                                     | `mixed`    | One archetype in seven has a bracket that pays for itself held out; InsideBar's stop is nearly inert and its forced flat hands back about 90% of what the bracket earns.                                                                                                          |
| `§M28.13` | [M28.13 — the registry read through an account, and the assumption that turned out to be a parameter](m28-13-account-read.md)       | `mixed`    | Survival is not the question and reading it as one inverts the answer; the binding constraint is position size rather than the strategy, and the excursion order was an assumption and is now `excursion_order`.                                                                  |
| `§M28.14` | [M28.14 — every stratum against its unfiltered twin, and the cell that survives it](m28-14-stratum-cross-read.md)                   | `mixed`    | The clock separates the registry while volume and trend mostly do not; the midday cell clears four gates and the flatten is still what earns it.                                                                                                                                  |
| `§M28.15` | [M28.15 — the midday cell through the three reads that stopped it being a recommendation](m28-15-midday-cell.md)                    | `mixed`    | Ten of ten walk-forward folds are profitable out of sample and the account funds on MNQ, but without the flatten there is no book to read — and 2026 remains the weakest year.                                                                                                    |
| `§M28.16` | [M28.16 — the ten consistent cells through the matched null, and what a consistency score is worth](m28-16-consistent-cells.md)     | `mixed`    | Four cells clear p = 0.05 on both roots — three OpeningRange's and one InsideBarTrailing's midday cell — and a consistency score does not order the null result, correlating −0.132 with it.                                                                                      |
| `§M29`    | [M29 — the maximum hold time: the one axis whose best value is off on every archetype](m29-maximum-hold-time.md)                    | `negative` | Capping a trade's length is a cost on all seven archetypes and the cost is monotone in the cap; the selection window picks a paying rung zero times in seven, and the two ported archetypes hold too briefly to reach one at all.                                                 |
| `§M30`    | [M30 — volume and regime re-cut across the registry, and what the raw pair was reporting](m30-volume-regime-recut.md)               | `mixed`    | Re-cutting turns three of six volume dimensions from inert to consistent and sorts the regime dimension by what each archetype is; almost none of the new cells makes money, and the raw regime labels agree with a calibrated cut about a fifth of the time at a lookback of 50. |

## Not about one archetype

Condition labels, thresholds and gate machinery. Every archetype is read through these, so a result that turns on one of them is really a result about the label.
